lines: init:  roll out with the hinted prompt until a trajectory passes (at most `init_attempts` tries)
move:  cut x at a uniformly random turn j, keep turns < j, regenerate turns >= j with the hinted prompt -> x';
-           reject x' if it does not pass; otherwise keep it when it scores at least as well as the current state
-           under the student, using the paper's length-normalised score (App. C.2),
-               s(x) = (1 / |x|) * sum_t log pi(x_t | x_<t, plain prompt)   over the policy's own tokens.
+           reject x' if it does not pass; otherwise keep it when the Metropolis-Hastings ratio for the
+           target above against this proposal is at least 1,
+               log alpha = [S(x') - S(x)] - [H_j(x') - H_j(x)] + log T - log T'  >=  0,
+           where S is the summed student log-prob over the policy's own tokens, H_j is the summed hinted
+           log-prob over the regenerated suffix (turns >= j), and T, T' are the turn counts of x, x'
+           (the reverse move must re-choose the same cut j). The H terms are essential: without them a
+           suffix the hinted policy over-proposes (e.g. copied from the gold query) looks just as good as
+           one the student would produce itself, and a length-normalised mean additionally favours long,
+           predictable narration over the student's own passing trajectories.
